authors: Claudio Mantuano, Olalekan Omoyele, Maximilian Hoffmann, Jann Michael Weinand, Massimo Panella, Detlef Stolten
title: Data imputation methods for intermittent renewable energy sources: Implications for energy system modeling
validity_discussion: Discusses how point-wise error (RMSE) fails to capture distribution preservation (KS test) and downstream validity in energy system optimization models. Key quote: "While certain imputation methods demonstrate strong point-wise statistical accuracy, they do not necessarily preserve the underlying data distribution."

authors: Yige Sun, Jing Li, Yifan Xu, Tingting Zhang, Xiaofeng Wang
title: Deep learning versus conventional methods for missing data imputation: A review and comparative study
validity_discussion: Evaluates validity under Rubin's framework (MCAR, MAR, MNAR), showing deep learning models (GAIN, VAE) suffer from mode collapse and bias under MAR/MNAR compared to MICE and missForest. Key quote: "The validity and effectiveness of imputation strategies are affected by missing mechanism, formalized by Rubin and colleagues (Little & Rubin, 2019; Rubin, 1976)... GAINs only perform well in the case of MCAR and often fail in the cases of MAR and MNAR."

title: Efficient Multiple Imputation for Diverse Data in Python and R: MIDASpy and rMIDAS
validity_discussion: Discusses combining multiple imputations using Rubin's rules to obtain valid standard errors and parameter estimates for post-imputation GLM analysis. Key quote: "Due to the relative paucity of multiple imputation software in Python, MIDASpy includes a function for estimating generalized linear regression models and combining the results according to the Rubin rules: combine()."

authors: Alexander Barth, Julien Brajard, Aida Alvera-Azcárate, Bayoumy Mohamed, Charles Troupin, Jean-Marie Beckers
title: Ensemble reconstruction of missing satellite data using a denoising diffusion model: application to chlorophyll a concentration in the Black Sea
validity_discussion: Evaluates probabilistic validity and reliability of reconstructed ensembles using Talagrand rank histograms and CRPS decomposition. Key quote: "The spatial scales of the reconstructed data are assessed via a variogram, and the accuracy and statistical validity of the reconstructed ensemble are quantified using the continuous ranked probability score and its decomposition into reliability, resolution, and uncertainty."

authors: Zachary K. Collier, Minji Kong, Olushola Soyoye, Kamal Chawla, Ann M. Aviles, Yasser Payne
title: Deep Learning Imputation for Asymmetric and Incomplete Likert-Type Items
validity_discussion: Discusses Rubin's mechanisms (MCAR, MAR, MNAR) and notes that naive traditional imputation (discriminant analysis, logistic regression) yields significant bias on skewed ordinal Likert items. Key quote: "The use of conventional techniques, such as discriminant analysis or logistic regression imputation, for handling missing data in asymmetric items may result in significant bias."
